title: Digital CIM with Noisy SRAM Bit: A Compact Clustered Annealer for Large-Scale Combinatorial Optimization
problem: Ising model-based annealers suffer from quadratic scaling in the number of spins, preventing efficient solution of large-scale traveling salesman problems with tens of thousands of cities. Conventional approaches require prohibitive memory resources that scale with problem size.
motivation: Combinatorial optimization problems like TSP are NP-hard and intractable on conventional CPUs, requiring efficient hardware accelerators to enable practical large-scale solutions.
method: This system uses a memory-based processor (where computation happens directly in storage, saving time), organized in nested groups to skip over empty spaces in the input data and zeros in the weight values (the parameters controlling the calculation). To generate the randomness needed for annealing, it exploits a quirk: SRAM chips running at below-normal power produce random bit errors from manufacturing imperfections during read operations—turning the chip's own noise into a feature. Engineers explored different cluster sizes and programmability levels to balance how well it solves problems against how much hardware it needs.
key_novelty: Instead of building a separate random-number generator, the system uses natural manufacturing imperfections in SRAM chips running at low power to create the randomness needed for the annealing algorithm.
contributions: Digital CIM-based clustered annealer architecture using SRAM for scalable TSP solving
Novel exploitation of SRAM process variations and noisy bits to implement stochastic annealing
Hierarchical clustering approach enabling solution of up to 85,900-city TSP with only megabytes of SRAM
Achieves >10^9× speedup versus CPU baseline with <25% solution quality overhead and >10^13× normalized area-power improvement over state-of-the-art annealers

metrics.speedup: >10^9× vs CPU baseline; >10^13× on normalized area-power vs SOTA

limitations: Solution quality degradation of up to 25% compared to CPU baseline; scalability to extremely large problem instances not fully characterized.
primary_theme: SRAM-based Ising annealer for large-scale TSP
